comments.text: The reversal you trace is striking — Belfast starting as the industrial centre with Harland and Wolff and the linen trade, then the Republic pulling ahead through export tax cuts and firms like Apple in Cork and Intel in Leixlip. How much of that swap do you think was driven by those policy choices, versus the loss of the North's shipbuilding and linen base itself?
